name: Indonesian Market Signals & Macro Context (consolidated: parent complaints about opaque report cards, Sparks Math ability-based placement as willingness-to-pay evidence, PISA/AKM scale of the numeracy problem, edtech TAM/SAM)
origin_region: Indonesia (national), calibrated against global benchmarks (OECD PISA 2022). Provider evidence is concentrated in Jabodetabek and the Java/Bali urban corridor: Sparks Math operates in Bintaro, Kelapa Gading, Kalimalang, Tebet and Bogor with announced expansion to Bandung, Bali, Sunter, Pekayon and Pulomas; Kumon prices across five geographic tiers with Jabodetabek & Karawang as the premium Area 1.
target_age: Primary focus SD (elementary, ages 6-12, Kelas 1-6), ~23.93 million students in the 2024/2025 odd semester. The macro indicators bracket this cohort from both sides: AKM/Asesmen Nasional measures Kelas 5 SD directly and is a census rather than a sample, while PISA measures 15-year-olds and therefore reads as a lagging indicator of SD-stage foundations. Paid tutoring providers cited serve overlapping bands: Sparks Math ages 3-13 (Tiny Explorer 3, Little Explorer 4-6, Critical Thinker 7-10, Brave Solver 10-13), Ruangguru Math Champs ages 5-14, Kumon preschool through senior high, CoLearn Kelas 5 SD upward.
delivery_mode: Split market with an inverted value/price relationship. Offline tutoring (bimbel/les) remains the dominant paid channel and sets the price anchor at roughly Rp 425,000-750,000 per subject per month; online-app edtech is the volume channel but has repeatedly failed to monetise at that level and prices an order of magnitude lower (CoLearn live bimbel Rp 90,000-170,000/month, Ruangguru Math Champs from ~Rp 280,000/month). The clearest evidence of that monetisation failure is Zenius, Indonesia's 20-year-old pioneer, announcing a temporary shutdown of services in January 2024 after reportedly burning ~USD 40M, following Ruangguru's layoffs of hundreds of employees in late 2022. Practical implication: parents pay premium prices for physical presence and a credible human progress narrative, not for content volume.
language_localization: Bahasa Indonesia is mandatory for the parent-facing layer, and the strongest evidence for this is that the headline parent pain point is itself a LANGUAGE failure rather than a data failure. Under Kurikulum Merdeka the SD report card is a narrative description with no red marks and no class ranking, and reporting repeatedly shows parents cannot decode it. Teachers are themselves documented as struggling to 'menerjemahkan capaian kompetensi menjadi deskripsi yang singkat, jelas' (translate competency attainment into short, clear descriptions), so the failure is bidirectional: the school cannot compress the diagnosis into plain language, and the parent cannot expand the description back into an actionable cause. Any product entering here must ship its output in parent-grade Bahasa Indonesia, not in pedagogical register.
pricing_model: Two established price anchors, both subscription. (1) Offline per-subject monthly: Kumon Indonesia preschool-SD Rp 430,000-525,000/subject/month plus a one-time Rp 300,000-350,000 registration (schedule effective 1 January 2026); Sparks Math 'mulai dari Rp 60 Ribuan per sesi atau Rp 500 Ribuan per bulan' (from ~Rp 60,000/session or ~Rp 500,000/month); Sakamoto Rp 425,000-750,000/month for ~8 sessions, or Rp 6.8-7.0 million for a 12-month package; Superprof marketplace tutors average ~Rp 81,000/hour in Jakarta. (2) Online/hybrid monthly: CoLearn Rp 90,000-170,000/month, Ruangguru Math Champs from ~Rp 280,000/month for packages including face-to-face interactive classes, escalating to Rp 4.0-4.5 million/month for intensive live teaching. Free trial classes and free placement tests are the standard acquisition offer across the offline segment (Sparks Math advertises daily free trial classes with new-enrolment discounts up to Rp 2,000,000; Kumon offers a free placement test and consultation).
local_curriculum_alignment: Kurikulum Merdeka is the governing frame and it creates genuine policy tailwind because it explicitly mandates asesmen diagnostik (diagnostic assessment) at the start of learning, defined as identifying learner capability 'agar guru dapat merancang pembelajaran yang sesuai' (so the teacher can design appropriate instruction). The tailwind is unrealised in practice: Indonesian studies of SD teacher competency find teachers 'masih mengalami kesulitan dalam menyusun instrumen asesmen yang sesuai' (still struggle to construct suitable assessment instruments), and systematic literature review of mathematics teachers implementing Kurikulum Merdeka finds multiple persistent implementation barriers. So the curriculum has already legitimised and named the exact job-to-be-done (diagnose before you teach) while leaving the instrument unbuilt. Notably, the premium offline providers deliberately run NON-aligned curricula: Sparks Math sells the Singapore curriculum with CPA (Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract) methodology and Bar Model, and Sakamoto and Kumon likewise sell imported methods, indicating parents treat local-curriculum alignment as optional when a method carries stronger perceived diagnostic credibility.
does_error_type_diagnosis: no — at the market level, nothing in the Indonesian mainstream (schools, bimbel, or apps) diagnoses error TYPE. The market-level ceiling is threefold and every layer stops short of the taxonomy. (1) SCHOOL: the Kurikulum Merdeka rapor produces narrative descriptors ending in phrases like 'Perlu bimbingan lebih lanjut' / 'Perlu mendapatkan bimbingan lagi untuk menemukan solusi' — a verdict without a cause. (2) OFFLINE TUTORING: the most sophisticated instrument in commercial use is the ability-based placement test, which maps LEVEL (where in the sequence the child belongs) rather than ERROR TYPE (which of reading, concept, or calculation is failing within a level). Kumon reduces mastery to accuracy plus Standard Completion Time; Sparks Math places by 'kemampuan aktual' and separately offers a 'Test Gaya Belajar Anak' (learning-style test), which is a learner-trait instrument, not an error-diagnostic one. (3) APPS: topic-mastery mapping at best. The single most telling artefact is that Sparks Math's own marketing content NAMES the three-way error taxonomy in prose — 'salah memahami soal, salah menerapkan rumus, atau kesalahan hitung yang tidak disengaja' — while shipping no instrument that measures it. The vocabulary of the gap already exists in Indonesian commercial copy; the measurement does not.
diagnosis_granularity: score-only at the school layer (narrative descriptors plus a numeric range), level-placement at the premium offline layer (ability-based placement test producing a starting point in a fixed worksheet/skill sequence), and topic-mastery-map at the strongest app layer. Nothing observed in the Indonesian market reaches mcq-distractor-mapped-misconception, let alone full-error-type-taxonomy. The national AKM/Asesmen Nasional layer is coarser still: it is reported as a single binary per domain — proportion of students reaching versus not reaching 'kompetensi minimum numerasi' — which is a one-bit diagnosis applied to a census of ~24 million SD students.
diagnosis_input_modality: Predominantly final-answer scoring: mcq and short-answer marked right/wrong. Offline providers are the only actors that routinely collect the child's handwritten working (Kumon collects step-by-step worksheets daily; CoLearn collects weekly non-multiple-choice handwritten exercises; Sparks Math runs in-person small groups of 10-15 where an instructor sees the work), but in every case that working is consumed by a human grader's eye and reduced to a score, a completion time, or an error count — never captured as classified data. This is the market's central waste: the richest diagnostic substrate in Indonesia is already being physically collected at scale and thrown away at the point of conversion into a parent report. No Indonesian provider observed uses handwriting-stroke capture or free-response OCR of the child's own attempt for diagnostic classification.
ai_tutor_diagnosis_reliability: Not directly applicable at the market level, because no Indonesian provider publishes an error-type diagnosis whose reliability could be validated. No Indonesian ground-truth validation study, no published inter-rater agreement, and no accuracy claim for any AI diagnosis was found for any Indonesian product. The relevant reliability caution therefore has to be imported from the frontier-research item in this outline (the 'Correct Answer Trap' / EDGE line of work showing frontier LLMs catch only ~57-84% of misconceptions when the reasoning is wrong but the final answer happens to be right). Applied to this market, that finding is doubly damaging: since the Indonesian mainstream diagnoses from the final answer alone, its effective misconception-detection reliability on correct-but-wrongly-reasoned items is approximately zero by construction. [uncertain]
evidence_quote: Three quotes carry the claim. (1) THE PARENT CANNOT READ THE VERDICT — from BIC's guide to Kurikulum Merdeka learning phases, a father described reading his child's report card that has no red marks, no ranking, only long descriptions ending in 'Perlu bimbingan lebih lanjut' (needs further guidance), asks: 'Anak saya ini pintar atau tidak, sih? Kok bahasanya muter-muter?' ('Is my child actually smart or not? Why does the language just go round in circles?'). (2) THE PARENT CANNOT EXPLAIN THE FAILURE DESPITE PAYING FOR EFFORT — from Sparks Math's own blog on why Kelas 6 children fail maths exams: 'Yang membuat banyak orang tua bingung adalah kenyataan bahwa anak mereka sudah belajar keras, sudah mengerjakan banyak latihan soal, tapi hasil ujiannya tetap tidak sesuai harapan.' ('What confuses many parents is the reality that their child has already studied hard and done many practice problems, yet the exam results still fall short of expectations.') (3) THE TAXONOMY IS NAMED BUT NOT MEASURED — the same Sparks Math article decomposes practice errors into 'salah memahami soal, salah menerapkan rumus, atau kesalahan hitung yang tidak disengaja' ('misunderstanding the problem, applying the wrong formula, or unintentional calculation mistakes') — a near-exact restatement of the B/K/H triad (Baca/Konsep/Hitung) appearing in Indonesian commercial marketing copy — while the only assessment the company actually offers the visitor is a 'Test Gaya Belajar Anak' (child's learning-style test). Naming the error types is already a selling proposition in Indonesia; measuring them is not yet a product.
how_parent_involved: gatekeeper + dashboard-consumer, with a documented willingness to spend both money and physical time on the reporting ritual itself. The parent is the payer and the installer of the app on an often-shared phone, and in the offline channel the parent is also an active participant: Kumon Indonesia enrolment begins with the parent booking an instructor appointment, attending a free learning consultation, then attending monthly parent orientation (orientasi orang tua) and supervising the daily at-home worksheet routine; Sparks Math schedules progress sheets and parent-teacher meetings at 1 and 3 months with further direct consultation at months 3 and 6. Online players push reports to the parent's WhatsApp (Ruangguru's monthly Laporan Belajar retrievable by texting 'Rapor Anak'; CoLearn's attendance and exam-readiness reports 'Langsung ke WhatsApp orang tua'). The uniform limitation across all of them is that what the parent receives is scores, topic names, attendance, completion times and error COUNTS — never an error TYPE, and never a script for what to do differently at home. The parent is positioned to observe and to pay, never to coach.
ai_tutor_directly_to_child: Mixed and trending toward yes, but without diagnosis attached. Ruangguru ships AiRIS, marketed as 'Tutor AI Smart dan Interaktif Pertama di Indonesia', chatting 24/7 directly with SD/SMP/SMA students; QANDA and Photomath answer the child directly. Against this, CoLearn's English-language CoTutor explicitly refuses a conversational channel with the child — 'Your child cannot have conversations with us. Interactions are limited to analyzing their questions and their work' — and gates answers behind a written attempt. The market signal is that direct-to-child AI conversation is now table stakes and is NOT a differentiator; the unclaimed position is diagnosis quality and the parent-facing explanation of it. [uncertain]
key_finding: Indonesia presents a rare combination of enormous problem scale, proven willingness-to-pay, explicit policy legitimation, and a completely unbuilt instrument — with the gap already named in the market's own marketing language. Five strands. (1) SCALE IS NATIONAL AND MEASURED, NOT ANECDOTAL. Indonesia scored 366 in PISA 2022 mathematics, ranking 69th of 81 participating countries against an international/OECD average of 472; only 18% of Indonesian students attained at least Level 2 proficiency in mathematics versus an OECD average of 69%, meaning roughly four in five Indonesian 15-year-olds cannot perform basic mathematical reasoning. Domestically the AKM/Asesmen Nasional census tells the same story earlier in the pipeline: the proportion of students reaching minimum NUMERACY competency was 45.24% (2022), 62.45% (2023) and 67.94% (2024) — improving fast, but still leaving about one-third of the ~23.93 million SD students below minimum numeracy in 2024. Critically for product positioning, the AKM verdict is one bit per child ('reached' / 'did not reach'), so even the government instrument tells a parent that their child failed without telling them why. (2) THE PARENT PAIN IS SPECIFICALLY A CAUSAL-ATTRIBUTION PAIN, NOT A SCORE PAIN. Kurikulum Merdeka removed red marks and ranking in favour of narrative descriptors, and the documented reaction is parents unable to locate their child's weakness: 'Anak saya ini pintar atau tidak, sih? Kok bahasanya muter-muter?', with reports terminating in generic guidance language such as 'Perlu bimbingan lebih lanjut'. The same attribution failure recurs at the tutoring layer — parents pay for effort (hard study, many practice problems, monthly bimbel) and still cannot explain the shortfall. Notably, teachers face the mirror-image problem, struggling to compress competency attainment into clear descriptions and, per Indonesian SD-competency studies, to construct suitable assessment instruments in the first place. (3) WILLINGNESS TO PAY FOR MORE PRECISE PLACEMENT IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT HYPOTHESISED. Sparks Math sells the Singapore curriculum with CPA and Bar Model to ages 3-13 at ~Rp 60,000/session or ~Rp 500,000/month, in physical branches across Jabodetabek and Bogor with announced expansion to Bandung and Bali, and its differentiator in its own FAQ is 'Penempatan berdasarkan kemampuan aktual' (placement based on actual ability) — indexed more fully as 'Placement Test Awal: Setiap siswa baru akan mengikuti placement test (tes penempatan) terlebih dahulu untuk memetakan pemahaman mereka. Penempatan Berbasis Kemampuan: Kami menempatkan siswa berdasarkan kemampuan (ability-based), bukan kaku berdasarkan usia atau level sekolah mereka saat ini' [uncertain: the extended wording comes from the search index of math.sparks-edu.com/lokasi/bandung/test-bernad/; the short FAQ phrase is directly verified on-site]. Kumon charges Rp 430,000-525,000 per subject per month for SD plus Rp 300,000-350,000 registration off the back of the same promise, and Sakamoto Rp 425,000-750,000/month. Indonesian urban parents therefore already pay roughly Rp 5-9 million per year, per subject, for an instrument that only resolves LEVEL. The pricing gradient is the proof: the market pays 3-6x more for offline level-placement (Rp 425,000-750,000/month) than for unlimited online content (CoLearn Rp 90,000-170,000/month), so the premium is being paid for perceived diagnostic precision and a human progress narrative, not for content. (4) THE GAP IS ALREADY ARTICULATED IN INDONESIAN COMMERCIAL COPY. Sparks Math's blog decomposes exam failure into 'salah memahami soal, salah menerapkan rumus, atau kesalahan hitung' — effectively B/K/H — yet the only assessment it actually offers is a learning-style test. A provider that can write the taxonomy but cannot sell the measurement is the cleanest possible demand signal: the concept needs no market education, only an instrument. (5) MARKET SIZE SUPPORTS A FOCUSED WEDGE, NOT A BROAD PLAY. TAM: the Indonesia edtech market is put at USD 3.23 billion (2024) growing to USD 8.81 billion by 2033 at 11.79% CAGR (IMARC), with a K-12 cloud-based edtech slice of USD 1.9 billion (2025) to USD 3.5 billion (2031) at 14.8% CAGR (Ken Research). SAM: the Indonesia online private tutoring market is valued at USD 1.3 billion (2025) (Ken Research). Bottom-up sanity check for an SD-maths diagnostic: ~23.93 million SD students, ~4 million per grade cohort; even 1% of a single grade cohort at the CoLearn-tier price of Rp 120,000/month implies ~Rp 58 billion/year (~USD 3.5 million) [uncertain: derived arithmetic, not a published figure]. The caution attached to this size is Zenius — a 20-year incumbent that suspended services in January 2024 after reportedly burning ~USD 40M, alongside Ruangguru's 2022 layoffs — which shows Indonesian consumers will not pay app-tier prices for undifferentiated content. The strategic reading is that the money in Indonesian SD maths sits in the offline price band and is released by diagnostic credibility plus a parent-legible report, and that a product should therefore be priced and positioned against Kumon/Sparks Math rather than against Ruangguru/CoLearn. [uncertain: vendor market-size estimates conflict materially — IMARC gives 11.79% CAGR for 'edtech' but 24.50% for 'online education' over the same window — so these figures should be treated as order-of-magnitude only.]
study_scale_or_sample: This item aggregates four bodies of evidence of very different weight. (1) PISA 2022 Indonesia — nationally representative sample survey: 13,439 students in 410 schools completed the mathematics, reading or science assessment, representing about 3,790,800 15-year-olds, roughly 85% of Indonesia's total 15-year-old population; conducted by OECD with standard sampling and weighting, so the 366 mathematics mean and the 18%-at-Level-2 figure are the strongest numbers in this record. (2) AKM / Asesmen Nasional & Rapor Pendidikan 2022-2024 — a national CENSUS rather than a sample, covering the full SD/SMP/SMA population (SD alone ~23.93 million students in the 2024/2025 odd semester), which is why the numeracy series (45.24% / 62.45% / 67.94%) is the highest-coverage evidence available, offset by extremely low granularity (one binary verdict per domain). (3) Provider pricing and placement evidence — a purposive sample of six named providers (Sparks Math, Kumon Indonesia, Sakamoto, Ruangguru Math Champs, CoLearn, Superprof), taken from official sites, published fee schedules effective 1 January 2026, and one provider-authored price-comparison article; commercially self-reported and therefore promotional in tone, though the Kumon fee schedule is an official published tariff. (4) Parent-complaint evidence — the weakest strand, and the honest limitation of this record: it rests on illustrative narrative vignettes in Indonesian education media and provider blogs rather than on a survey. No large-n Indonesian survey quantifying parental comprehension of the Kurikulum Merdeka narrative rapor was located; the nearest quantitative proxies are small and off-target (e.g. an IKIP Siliwangi study finding 46.6% of parents understood the 'merdeka' concept, n=30 PAUD parents in Bandung, and a JPTAM study of parental perception with n=10). Market-size figures are third-party commercial estimates (IMARC, Ken Research, 6Wresearch) with undisclosed methodology.
evidence_strength: moderate overall, but sharply uneven by strand and this unevenness is the key thing to carry forward. STRONG: the macro scale of the numeracy problem (PISA 2022 is a properly sampled international assessment; AKM is a national census) and the price anchors (Kumon's official published fee schedule effective 1 January 2026 is documentary evidence, not a claim). MODERATE: the willingness-to-pay inference — Sparks Math's ability-based placement is verified on the company's own site and its price point is published, and the 3-6x offline-over-online price premium is a real observed gradient, but the causal attribution of that premium specifically to diagnostic precision (rather than to supervision, discipline, physical convenience or brand) is an inference, not a measured elasticity. WEAK / ANECDOTAL: the parent-complaint strand, which is vignette-based (a named parent quote in an education-media article plus a provider blog's framing of parental confusion) and vulnerable to the objection that a tutoring company describing parental confusion is marketing rather than evidence — though the same framing appearing independently in non-commercial education media raises confidence. UNRESOLVED: the market-size figures, where vendor estimates conflict materially and no methodology is disclosed. The single strongest defensible claim in this record is the CONTRAST: nationally measured mass failure (82% of 15-year-olds below Level 2 maths, ~32% of SD students below minimum numeracy) sitting alongside a paid market whose most advanced commercial instrument resolves only LEVEL, not error type.
remediation_efficacy_evidence: None found for Indonesia — and this absence should be treated as a genuine finding and a genuine risk, not as a gap in searching. No Indonesian RCT or quasi-experiment was located showing that any diagnostic instrument in market use (Kumon's placement test plus Standard Completion Time, Sparks Math's ability-based placement test, Ruangguru Math Champs' monthly placement and progression testing, or any app's topic-mastery map) causally improves SD mathematics learning outcomes relative to a control. What exists domestically is national trend data with no counterfactual: minimum numeracy competency rose 45.24% to 67.94% between 2022 and 2024, but that period coincides with the Kurikulum Merdeka rollout and post-pandemic recovery, so it cannot be attributed to diagnostic practice, and the Rapor Pendidikan series is not designed to support causal inference. On the policy side, Kurikulum Merdeka mandates asesmen diagnostik but Indonesian studies report SD teachers still struggling to construct suitable assessment instruments and mathematics teachers facing persistent implementation barriers, so even the mandated diagnostic is not evidenced as delivered, let alone as effective. The applicable efficacy evidence must therefore be imported, and it cuts both ways: Eedi's EEF-evaluated distractor-mapped misconception approach is the positive precedent, while the Cognitive Tutor/ASSISTments literature carries the decisive caution that surfacing an error diagnosis is NOT sufficient — without well-designed remediation attached, diagnostic messaging alone does not move outcomes. For a B/K/H product this converts into a hard product requirement rather than a research footnote: the error-type label is the input to the intervention, not the deliverable, and the parent-facing output must be a specific next action in plain Bahasa Indonesia rather than a classification. It is also the obvious first experiment to run domestically, since no competitor has published one. [uncertain: this is an evidenced absence after targeted searching, not a proof that no such study exists — Indonesian-language dissertation and local-journal literature is poorly indexed in the engines used.]
